page: Microsoft Azure D96ds_v7 is a general-purpose server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor built on the x86_64 architecture. It features 96 dedicated virtual CPUs across 48 physical cores with hyper-threading, operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The processor is equipped with a 480 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets, including Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512. The instance is configured with 384 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU.

This instance includes 5669 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, making it highly capable for data-intensive operations. In benchmark evaluations, the D96ds_v7 demonstrates top-tier multi-threaded performance, achieving a Passmark CPU score of 106,546.32 and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 596.61 GB/sec. Its memory subsystem delivers a read-only cached bandwidth of 7,269.34 GB/sec. Database and web serving capabilities are also strong, with Redis SET operations reaching 156.15 million operations per second and static web serving throughput measured at 151.5 GB/sec.

The combination of high-frequency dedicated cores, massive local NVMe storage, and advanced matrix math extensions makes the D96ds_v7 well-suited for large-scale relational databases, high-throughput web serving, and CPU-based machine learning inference, such as medium-to-large LLM prompt processing. While it lacks a dedicated GPU, its AMX instruction support mitigates some vector processing limitations. The server offers high resource density and strong performance-per-core metrics, representing a balanced cost-to-performance profile for enterprise-grade workloads requiring local scratch space.
